Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Personal history of hyperthyroidism; occupation in high-stress environment (law).
- Precipitating factors: Recent job change with increased stress coincides with onset of symptoms.
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing job-related stress, persistent somatic symptoms impacting work and functioning.
- Protective factors: Good insight, engaged with healthcare, willing to seek in-person follow-up.
- Contributing factors: Multiple somatic complaints (headache, palpitations, tingling, weight/appetite loss, libido loss) temporally related to increased stress; possible overlap with endocrine dysfunction (hyperthyroidism); lifestyle change (job).

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Chronic stress/anxiety with somatic symptoms
- Patient Goal(s): Regain control over symptoms, improve well-being and work functioning
- Clinical Goal(s): Clarify etiology of somatic symptoms, reduce distress, monitor for anxiety or mood disorder
- Actions (Patient): Attend in-person review, monitor symptoms, avoid alcohol excess, consider stress management techniques
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Book in-person assessment, perform physical examination, order blood tests (including thyroid function), consider referral for psychological support if indicated

Secondary Problem: Hyperthyroidism (or over-replacement)
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain thyroid health, minimize physical/anxiety symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s): Assess for thyroid hormone imbalance, optimize therapy, monitor for side effects
- Actions (Patient): Continue current medication as prescribed, attend for blood tests, report new symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Order thyroid function tests, review medication dosage and adherence

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: No. Topics Covered: Not recorded
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalation of headaches, persistent palpitations, worsening anxiety, significant weight changes, impaired daily functioning
- Coping Strategies: Monitor stress, seek support as needed, use stress management/relaxation techniques if advised

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Hyperthyroidism (or over-replacement with thyroxine): High likelihood. Justification: Many symptoms (palpitations, weight loss, hot sensation, appetite/mood/libido changes) consistent with excessive thyroid hormone; known past history and current thyroxine use.
- Chronic stress/anxiety (with somatic symptoms): Medium likelihood. Justification: New onset of multiple somatic symptoms and high stress temporally associated with recent job change; symptoms align with anxiety/somatic spectrum.
- Migraine (possibly with aura): Medium likelihood. Justification: Severe, intermittent frontal headaches with occasional nausea and tingling in hands (possible aura or hyperventilation).

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Mental status examination, risk assessment (suicide/self-harm), sleep, social supports, consent, review arrangements—Not recorded in transcript or DDx.
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified; anxiety/stress and hyperthyroidism both supported by transcript and ranked DDx.
● Transcript quality notes: Some relevant social and mental health history not specifically probed; transcript largely focused on physical symptoms and medical rule-out. No formal mental health screen conducted.
